knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Strided CUDA tensor memory layout leads to incorrect kernel results
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Kernel and backend implementations may rely on hidden memory layout assumptions; when input tensors are non-contiguous with non-unit strides, offset calculations can produce incorrect values or indices.

risk_dimensions.shape: Strided views with logical shapes that differ from storage, including slicing with step greater than one, transposition, narrowing, or other stride-changing operations
risk_dimensions.dtype: Various dtypes may expose stride indexing or offset issues; no single dtype is assumed to be safe
risk_dimensions.memory: Non-contiguous memory layouts with stride greater than one, custom offsets, and view-derived tensors
risk_dimensions.device: CUDA GPU tensors and operations dispatched to GPU kernels
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Order-statistic or reduction-like operations called on non-contiguous GPU tensors

failure_mechanism.description: GPU kernel implementations may assume contiguous memory or incorrectly compute offsets for strided tensors, leading to wrong output values and index positions while the operation completes without immediate error.

input_exploration: Generate non-contiguous strided views from contiguous tensors using slicing, transpose, narrow, and other stride-changing operations
Vary shapes including small, large, degenerate, and uneven dimensions
Explore stride patterns with step greater than one, offset views, and negative strides
Test across different dtypes and CUDA device configurations
constraint_awareness: Keep selection or reduction parameters within valid dimension bounds for the current logical shape
Build reference results using the same logical tensor semantics, preferably from a contiguous tensor or CPU reference
Do not assume that non-contiguous and contiguous tensors follow identical execution paths
oracle_strategy: Compare returned values and indices against a contiguous tensor or CPU reference
Treat any value or index mismatch as a potential incorrect-output failure
Monitor crashes, sanitizer failures, and internal assertion errors

transferability.reason: Memory layout assumptions affect many tensor operations beyond order-statistic kernels, especially reductions, indexing, and GPU kernels that receive strided views. Testing non-contiguous CUDA tensors can reveal similar hidden stride handling bugs in other APIs.

important_considerations: Focus on non-contiguous memory layouts rather than only unusual shapes
Use stride-changing view operations to expose hidden kernel offset assumptions
Always compare against a contiguous or CPU reference to detect subtle wrong results
Consider GPU-specific execution paths when designing harnesses
generation_strategy: Create general harness variants that combine non-contiguous view construction, valid parameter bounds, and differential comparison against contiguous reference results. Use this knowledge to guide input generation for APIs that accept tensor inputs and may dispatch to shape- or stride-sensitive kernels.
